posts.text: getting home and immediately changing into the ‘house clothes’ is the only thing keeping society functioning.

perfume is an accessory. 

if your scent doesn’t match the mood of your outfit, you aren't done getting dressed.
the best outfits always happen when you have absolutely nowhere to be.
buying things in your size is one thing, but knowing your actual body measurements is the secret gatekeeping everyone ignores.
wearing socks with sandals is a personality test and i’m judging everyone who says no.
the people who film their outfits for social media usually look the least comfortable in real life.
having a dedicated 'errand outfit' is just a way to pretend we aren't all just doing the same mundane chores.
getting dressed in the dark during winter is the ultimate test of your personal style.

if you still own a single piece of clothing that has a ‘dry clean only’ tag, you are living a lie. 

it’s going in the wash.

tailoring everything you buy: 

obsessive control issue or just basic respect for your own body?
people who iron their jeans are the reason the rest of us feel like we’re falling behind.
the ‘third piece’ rule is just a gatekeeping tactic for people who want to feel superior about throwing on a belt.

there is a very specific type of person who buys clothes purely for the photo op, wears them once, and never thinks about them again. 

i don’t understand you.

wearing heels to the grocery store. 

brave, delusional, or just bored?
the ‘capsule wardrobe’ is just a fancy term for being afraid to have a personality in your closet.

people who keep the tags on their new clothes for days just to admire them. 

i see you.

buying a piece of clothing purely because it makes your silhouette look different. 

weird habit or genius strategy?
there is nothing more humbling than realizing your favorite outfit is actually just the same three silhouettes on rotation.

wearing pajamas out as a formal choice.

is it high-fashion bravery or just giving up?
the most judgmental people are the ones who swear they 'don't notice' what other women are wearing.

people who iron their clothes versus those who use a steamer.

which side of history are you on?
having that one item you bought four years ago that you refuse to toss because you might 'need it for a specific aesthetic' one day.
there is a specific vibe shift that happens the second you put on a coat that actually fits your shoulders properly.

you either get ready by picking the shoes first or you pick them last. 

there is no middle ground, pick your side.

everyone has that one piece of clothing they’re terrified to wear because they don’t think they’re ‘cool enough’ yet. 

stop waiting for a personality upgrade and just put it on.
owning clothes you’ve never worn is just a collection of your past selves you’re not ready to let go of.
the most stylish people i know are usually the ones who hate shopping the most.
if you spend more time planning the outfit than actually being at the event, you’re doing it right.

people who fold their clothes by category vs people who just throw them in a drawer.

which side are you on?
nothing ruins a good outfit faster than realizing you have to carry a bag that doesn't match the energy.
everyone claims they dress for comfort until a social event shows up on the calendar.
the weirdest part of growing up is realizing you actually like the clothes your mom told you not to wear.
the women who wear bright colors in the middle of winter are hiding a chaotic secret.
women who claim they ‘don’t have anything to wear’ while staring at a closet full of clothes are just bored, not broke.

perfume is an accessory. 

if you can smell someone from across the room, you’ve already failed.

sleeve length is the only thing that matters. 

too short or too long? 

it’s over.
the ‘i’m just going to try this on’ trap that ends with a two-hour closet overhaul at midnight.
the absolute audacity of a zipper breaking when you are already five minutes late.
the only people who actually believe black is the most versatile color are the ones who are afraid of texture.
the women who wear sunglasses inside aren't rude, they’re just protecting their peace from the fluorescent lighting.
realizing your outfit is uncomfortable five minutes after leaving the house is a special kind of betrayal.

thrifting for the thrill versus thrifting for the fit.

if you aren't digging through bins for three hours, are you even doing it right?
tailoring is just admitting you care more about your silhouette than your bank account.
the most judgmental people at a party aren't the ones in high fashion. they're the ones in oversized loungewear.
everyone claims to love their personal style until they look at a photo of themselves from three years ago.

wearing a coat inside: 

a sign of extreme style 

or just someone who is chronically cold?
if you never repeat an outfit for a social event, you aren't stylish. you're just stressed.
some of us use fashion to hide from the world. others use it to demand a seat at the table.

wearing heels to a grocery store: 

main character energy 

or just seeking attention?
buying clothes for the version of yourself you’re pretending to be next month is a full-time hobby.
the most interesting people in the room are always wearing the most basic shirt you’ve ever seen. explain why.
if you can’t sit cross-legged in your outfit, it wasn’t worth the money.
there is a specific type of person who buys an entire outfit just to wear it once for a photo. we see you.

oversized blazer or a structured cropped jacket.

pick one and tell me why you’re right.

most people don't actually hate trends.

they just hate that they can't pull them off like the people they follow.
the secret to looking expensive is knowing exactly when to stop adding accessories.
nothing humbles you faster than realizing your ‘signature style’ is just the same three silhouettes on repeat.

ironing a shirt is a personality type.

we can’t be friends with the people who just let the wrinkles happen.
people who claim they don’t care about brands are usually wearing the most expensive basic t-shirt in the room.
that weird stage of your life where you stop buying clothes because you’re waiting for a 'new version' of yourself to arrive.

dressing for the weather vs. dressing for the outfit you wish you were wearing.

which one are you winning?
women who keep their tags on until they leave the house are the only ones holding society together.
the panic when you realize you’ve worn the exact same color palette for five days straight.

you either love the chaos of mixing patterns or you’re a coward. 

there is no middle ground.

the best outfits don’t come from a mood board.

they come from the desperation of having nothing clean to wear.
the physical pain of having to change out of your favorite clothes just because it’s time to sleep.
if you think you can pull off socks with sandals, we need to have a serious conversation about your decision-making skills.
that moment when you see someone wearing your ‘unique’ piece and your whole personality suddenly feels less original.

wearing black from head to toe isn't a personality trait.

it's just a refusal to engage with color.
layering sweaters over dresses: genius move or just heat exhaustion waiting to happen?

everyone has that one piece of clothing they’re terrified to wash.

what’s yours?
you can tell how someone’s week is going by the amount of fabric they’re wearing.
the best outfit you’ve ever put together was probably an accident.

wearing heels to the airport isn't a flex.

it’s a cry for help.

you don’t actually like the trend.

you just like the lifestyle the person wearing it is selling you.

belt with loops or no belt at all.

there is no in-between.
the thrift store find that you lie about the price of is the only thing that matters in your closet.
the effort it takes to look like you didn't try at all is honestly exhausting.

oversized blazer or cropped jacket. 

pick one and tell me why you’re right.
the ‘outfit repeating’ stigma is a lie invented by people who don't know how to style their clothes.
everyone claims to hate fast fashion until it’s time to find a last minute birthday dinner dress.
the true test of your style is wearing what you love in a room full of people wearing the complete opposite.
getting dressed when you’re annoyed is usually when your best fits happen.
staring at a closet full of clothes and feeling like you have nothing to wear is a form of psychological warfare.

you’re either a ‘one signature scent’ person or someone who changes their perfume based on the outfit.

which side are you on?
the most judgmental people in any room are the ones wearing the most uncomfortable shoes.
people who iron their pajamas are hiding a level of chaos most of us aren't ready to witness.
never trust a girl who doesn't have a 'bad outfit' folder in her camera roll.

buying things in your size vs. buying the size that actually fits your shoulders. 

most of you are lying to yourselves.

the ‘going out’ top is officially dead.

if you aren’t wearing a button-down, you aren’t trying.

folding your clothes perfectly or shoving them into a drawer like a savage.

there is no in-between.
the internal panic when you see someone else wearing your exact fit in public is real.
wearing bright colors in the middle of a grey winter is a power move that i’m not brave enough for.
the ‘french girl’ aesthetic is just an excuse to wear neutral colors because you’re scared of a bad outfit.
the people who buy an entire outfit exactly as it’s styled on the mannequin are just outsourcing their personality.

keeping the tags on until you leave the house or ripping them off at the register. 

there is a moral divide here.
if you think clothes don’t change your mood, you’re clearly wearing the wrong things.
everyone claims they dress for comfort until they find a skirt that makes them feel like the main character.

thrift store hunters vs. department store regulars. 

only one of you actually knows how to build a real wardrobe.

people who keep their clothes strictly color-coded in their closet aren't organized. 

they're just bored.
